newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK COURT RULES AGAINST PRIVATISATION AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK COURT RULES AGAINST PRIVATISATION AGENCY.

text.p: The Slovak Constitutional Court on Thursday ruled the government, and not the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), is responsible for the direct sale of state property.
Under the current law, adopted in 1994, decisions on direct sales of state property are to be made by the NPF. Previously direct state sell-offs were the responsibility of the government.
"The court ruled the present law is unconstitutional," Mariana Mochnacova, the court's spokeswoman told Reuters.
"The Constitution says that the government has to decide on basic measures in economic and social politics," she added in a phone interview from Kosice, eastern Slovakia, the seat of the court.
Privatisation has been one of the hottest issues in Slovakia after a series of murky selloffs by the NPF.
The agency is currently run by supporters of Meciar's Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) and is accused by the opposition of cronyism in direct privatisation sales to investors.

The current privatisation law was supposed to put the NPF out of the reach of both the government and the anti-monopoly bureau, but was the subject of criticism because it allowed arbitrary direct sales of state property even to undisclosed individuals at prices unrelated to the market.
The court ruling effectively puts the control of direct sales decisions back into the government's hands, though it leaves the day-to-day administration of state property with the NPF.
